segs: SUCCESS CRITERIA:
VIEWING GOD AT WORK
MARK GAUTHIER
This article was written by Mark Gauthier to
Missionalteam leaders to give perspective and
explanation on the changes in the statistics made by
the National team fall of 2006. We want you to hear the
heart of why we record God’s work on our campuses. We
also think it is essential that you know what we have
chosen to measure and why we believe it is important.

So also in the New Testament, the first disciples
recorded (for example, the book of Acts) and reported
God at work through their ministry.
CELEBRATING THE WORKS OF GOD
Throughout the ages, the works of God have been a
cause for celebration and the foundation of faith for
God’s people. In the Old Testament, the Psalmists’
example spurs us to:
“...and they declared all that God had done with them,
and how he had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.”
(Acts 14:27; ESV)
“...they were welcomed by the church and the apostles
and elders, to whom they reported everything God had
done through them.” (Acts 15:4)
Commemorate the Works of God
Commemorate: To keep in people’s memories
Along with the inherent value for stimulating our
worship and faith, recording and reporting how God is
at work also has leadership value.
I will remember the deeds of the Lord; yes, I will
remember your miracles of long ago. [Psalm 77:11]

Meditate on the Works of God
Meditate: To think deeply about.
I will meditate on all your works and consider all your
might deeds. [Psalm 77:12] Great are the works of the
Lord; they are pondered (or studied; ESV) by all who
delight in them. [Psalm 111:2]
LEADERS LEAD
From honest evaluation
A key role of the leader is to embrace the reality that
comes from accurate measurements. Evaluating those
measurements enables us to identify areas where
God is obviously working and where we need to see
change.
Celebrate the Works of God
Celebrate: To mark with rejoicing and praise
For you make me glad by your deeds, O Lord; I sing for
joy at the works of your hands. [Psalm 92:4]
Toward increasing fruitfulness
Reality is the fertile ground for change. As we live out
the roles and responsibilities of a leader, knowing
the facts is a key in enabling us to lead toward greater
effectiveness.

In light of the whole
We are each called to live and lead in light of the whole
of the task we have been given. Measurements enable
us to be wise and faithful stewards of our campuses,

OUR SUCCESS CRITERIA
The following represents the Success Criteria of the
US Campus Ministry.
Personal and Group Evangelism
How many people have heard the gospel through
personal evangelism? (Includes both staff and student
evangelism and personal internet evangelism.)
What was the total number of people who heard the
gospel through group evangelism? (For instance: team
meetings; evangelistic presentations; etc.)
Media Exposures
How many people have been exposed to significant
gospel content with opportunities to respond in the
last month through media exposures?
(For instance: myeverystudent.com/ES.com, FSKs;
Bible, book or magazine giveaways; etc.)
Decisions for Christ
How many people have indicated a decision to receive
Christ as their Savior and Lord?
Multipliers
How many students are currently involved in spiritual
multiplication at the most organic level? That is: (a)
seeking to grow in Christ; and (b) seeking to share
their faith and pass on to others the foundational
concepts of the Christian living they are receiving?
Student Leaders
How many student leaders are leading small groups
of Win, Build, Send ministry? (For instance: groups
focused on reaching target audiences, launching
movements, etc)
The following numbers will be updated at the end of
the semester/quarter or as changes occur.
Movement Profiles
Movement definition: A leader with five aligned
students involved in Win, Build, and Send on the
most organic level. We are measuring the number of
movements planted in order to get to the scope of our
mission.
Number of Students Regularly Involved in Cru
Number of Laborers Sent
A graduated Christ-centered laborer is someone who
is growing in his/her faith, is multiplying his/her life,
and has been sent with a personal strategy to help
fulfill the Great Commission.
Additional Notes
You will note several significant changes in these
criteria. Two in particular may need additional
information.
The omission of the Involved New Believer statistic
In the 1990’s this statistic was added in order to solve
the systemic problem of students’ lack of engagement
in the mission. We believed that by measuring the end
result of evangelistic efforts it would actually increase
our effectiveness in seeing students come to Christ
and get involved in our ministry. While this is a very
good statistic, almost 15 years later we find we have
the same problem to solve. Now what we are doing is
measuring several key events in the process of seeing
a student become involved in our mission, instead of
assuming those events.
The definition of Laborers Sent
It has always been our passion as a movement to
“send” each and every student as a Christ- centered
laborer. We want to more accurately measure our
effectiveness in doing this. This number still includes
the number of staff, stinters and interns Joining with
us, which is vital to the growth of our movement and
the accomplishment of the mission to which God has
called us.
